evidence.quote: However, the distribution pattern of many individual particles mimics the diffraction pattern produced by waves.

assertions.statement: The distribution pattern of many individual particles mimics the diffraction pattern produced by waves.

evidence.quote: the double-slit experiment was seen as a demonstration of the wave nature of light.

assertions.statement: The double-slit experiment was seen as a demonstration of the wave nature of light.

evidence.quote: Thus it has been demonstrated that all matter possesses wave characteristics.

assertions.statement: The source says that the observation of the same type of interference pattern in experiments using matter demonstrates that all matter possesses wave characteristics.

evidence.quote: a beam of light is directed through two narrow, closely spaced slits, producing an interference pattern of light and dark bands on a screen.

assertions.statement: The double-slit experiment produces an interference pattern of light and dark bands when a beam of light is directed through two narrow, closely spaced slits.

evidence.quote: If the source intensity is turned down, the same interference pattern will slowly build up, one "count" or particle (e.g. photon or electron) at a time.

assertions.statement: When the source intensity is reduced, the interference pattern builds up one particle at a time, including photons or electrons.

evidence.quote: The concept of wave–particle duality says that neither the classical concept of "particle" nor of "wave" can fully describe the behavior of quantum-scale objects, either photons or matter.

assertions.statement: Wave–particle duality says that neither the classical concept of a particle nor the classical concept of a wave can fully describe quantum-scale objects, including photons and matter.

evidence.quote: Wave–particle duality is an example of the principle of complementarity in quantum physics.

assertions.statement: Wave–particle duality is an example of the principle of complementarity in quantum physics.

evidence.quote: The quantum system acts as a wave when passing through the double slits, but as a particle when it is detected.

assertions.statement: In the double-slit experiment, the quantum system acts as a wave when passing through the double slits and as a particle when detected.

evidence.quote: Variations of the double-slit experiment have been performed using electrons, atoms, and even large molecules, and the same type of interference pattern is seen.

assertions.statement: Variations of the double-slit experiment using electrons and atoms produce the same type of interference pattern.
